sanskrit: ayaṃ vai dānavo brahmann ilvalo vasumān bhuvi tam abhikramya sarve 'dya vayaṃ yācāmahe vasu
english: O brahmin, this demon Ilvala is truly wealthy on earth. Approaching him together, today we shall all beg wealth from him.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tadāsīd rucitam ilvalasyopabhikṣaṇam tatas te sahitā rājann ilvalaṃ samupādravan
english: That plan to beg from Ilvala was pleasing to all of them. Then, O king, they together approached Ilvala.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca ilvalas tān viditvā tu maharṣisahitān nṛpān upasthitān sahāmātyo viṣayānte 'bhyapūjayat
english: Lomaśa said: Knowing that the kings accompanied by the great sage had arrived, Ilvala, together with his ministers, honored them at the border of his realm.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tato 'suraśreṣṭha ātithyam akarot tadā sa saṃskṛtena kauravya bhrātrā vātāpinā kila
english: Then that foremost of demons, O Kaurava, performed hospitality for them — indeed with his brother Vātāpi, who had been cooked and prepared.

sanskrit: tato rājarṣayaḥ sarve viṣaṇṇā gatacetasaḥ vātāpiṃ saṃskṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā meṣabhūtaṃ mahāsuram
english: Then all the royal sages became dejected and lost heart upon seeing the great demon Vātāpi, who had been transformed into a ram and cooked.

sanskrit: athābravīd agastyas tān rājarṣīn ṛṣisattamaḥ viṣādo vo na kartavyo ahaṃ bhokṣye mahāsuram
english: Then Agastya, foremost of sages, spoke to those royal sages: "You must not be despondent. I myself shall consume the great demon."

sanskrit: dhuryāsanam athāsādya niṣasāda mahāmuniḥ taṃ paryaveṣad daityendra ilvalaḥ prahasann iva
english: The great sage then took his seat at the head-place and sat down. Ilvala, lord of the Daityas, served him, as if smiling.

sanskrit: agastya eva kṛtsnaṃ tu vātāpiṃ bubhuje tataḥ bhuktavaty asuro ''hvānam akarot tasya ilvalaḥ
english: Agastya alone then ate Vātāpi in his entirety. When the sage had finished eating, Ilvala called out to his brother.

sanskrit: tato vāyuḥ prādurabhūd agastyasya mahātmanaḥ ilvalaś ca viṣaṇṇo 'bhūd dṛṣṭvā jīrṇaṃ mahāsuram
english: Then a wind emerged from the great-souled Agastya, and Ilvala became distressed upon seeing the great demon had been digested.

sanskrit: prāñjaliś ca sahāmātyair idaṃ vacanam abravīt kimartham upayātāḥ stha brūta kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ
english: With folded hands, together with his ministers, he spoke these words: "For what purpose have you come? Speak — what may I do for you?"

sanskrit: pratyuvāca tato 'gastyaḥ prahasann ilvalaṃ tadā īśaṃ hy asura vidmas tvāṃ vayaṃ sarve dhaneśvaram
english: Then Agastya replied to Ilvala with a smile: "O demon, we all know you to be a lord, a master of wealth."

sanskrit: ime ca nātidhanino dhanārthaś ca mahān mama yathāśakty avihiṃsyānyān saṃvibhāgaṃ prayaccha naḥ
english: "These kings here are not overly wealthy, and my own need for wealth is great. Give us a share according to your capacity, without injuring others."

sanskrit: tato 'bhivādya tam ṛṣim ilvalo vākyam abravīt ditsitaṃ yadi vetsi tvaṃ tato dāsyāmi te vasu
english: Then Ilvala, bowing to the sage, spoke these words: "If you know what I intend to give, then I will give you that wealth."

sanskrit: agastya uvāca gavāṃ daśa sahasrāṇi rājñām ekaikaśo 'sura tāvad eva suvarṇasya ditsitaṃ te mahāsura
english: Agastya said: "Ten thousand cows for each of the kings, O demon, and that same amount in gold — that is what you intend to give, O great demon."

sanskrit: mahyaṃ tato vai dviguṇaṃ rathaś caiva hiraṇmayaḥ manojavau vājinau ca ditsitaṃ te mahāsura jijñāsyatāṃ rathaḥ sadyo vyaktam eṣa hiraṇmayaḥ
english: "And for me, twice that amount, plus a golden chariot and two horses swift as thought — that is what you intend to give, O great demon. Let the chariot be examined at once; it will be evident this one is golden."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca jijñāsyamānaḥ sa rathaḥ kaunteyāsīd dhiraṇmayaḥ tataḥ pravyathito daityo dadāv abhyadhikaṃ vasu
english: Lomaśa said: When examined, that chariot proved to be made of gold, O son of Kuntī. Then the demon, distressed, gave even more than the specified wealth.

sanskrit: vivājaś ca suvājaś ca tasmin yuktau rathe hayau ūhatus tau vasūny āśu tāny agastyāśramaṃ prati sarvān rājñaḥ sahāgastyān nimeṣād iva bhārata
english: The two horses named Vivaja and Suvaja, yoked to that chariot, swiftly carried all those riches toward Agastya's hermitage, along with all the kings and Agastya himself, as if in the blink of an eye, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: agastyenābhyanujñātā jagmū rājarṣayas tadā kṛtavāṃś ca muniḥ sarvaṃ lopāmudrācikīrṣitam
english: Dismissed by Agastya, the royal sages departed. And the sage did everything that Lopamudra had desired.

sanskrit: lopāmudrovāca kṛtavān asi tat sarvaṃ bhagavan mama kāṅkṣitam utpādaya sakṛn mahyam apatyaṃ vīryavattaram
english: Lopamudra said: "You have done all that I desired, O blessed one. Now beget for me a single offspring endowed with great valor."

sanskrit: agastya uvāca tuṣṭo 'ham asmi kalyāṇi tava vṛttena śobhane vicāraṇām apatye tu tava vakṣyāmi tāṃ śṛṇu
english: Agastya said: "I am pleased, O auspicious and beautiful one, with your conduct. But regarding offspring, I shall offer you a consideration — listen to it."

sanskrit: sahasraṃ te 'stu putrāṇāṃ śataṃ vā daśasaṃmitam daśa vā śatatulyāḥ syur eko vāpi sahasravat
english: "Do you wish for a thousand sons, or a hundred equal to ten, or ten equal to a hundred, or one who shall be equal to a thousand?"

sanskrit: lopāmudrovāca sahasrasaṃmitaḥ putra eko me 'stu tapodhana eko hi bahubhiḥ śreyān vidvān sādhur asādhubhiḥ
english: Lopamudra said: "Let me have one son equal to a thousand, O you whose wealth is asceticism. For one learned and virtuous person is better than many who are not."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca sa tatheti pratijñāya tayā samabhavan muniḥ samaye samaśīlinyā śraddhāvāñ śraddadhānayā
english: Lomaśa said: Having agreed with the words "So be it," the sage united with her in due season — she who was of equal virtue, full of faith and devotion.

sanskrit: tata ādhāya garbhaṃ tam agamad vanam eva saḥ tasmin vanagate garbho vavṛdhe sapta śāradān
english: Then, having planted the embryo, he went back into the forest. In the forest that embryo grew for seven autumns.

sanskrit: saptame 'bde gate cāpi prācyavat sa mahākaviḥ jvalann iva prabhāvena dṛḍhasyur nāma bhārata sāṅgopaniṣadān vedāñ japann eva mahāyaśāḥ
english: And when the seventh year had passed, that great poet was born just as Pracyavana was — blazing with power, named Dridhasyu, O Bhārata, of great renown, chanting the Vedas with their supplements and Upaniṣads even at birth.

sanskrit: tasya putro 'bhavad ṛṣeḥ sa tejasvī mahān ṛṣiḥ sa bāla eva tejasvī pitus tasya niveśane idhmānāṃ bhāram ājahre idhmavāhas tato 'bhavat
english: That son of the sage became a radiant, great sage. Even as a child, full of brilliance, he would bring loads of firewood to his father's dwelling — hence he came to be called Idhmavaha, the firewood-carrier.

sanskrit: tathāyuktaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā mumude sa munis tadā lebhire pitaraś cāsya lokān rājan yathepsitān
english: Seeing him thus engaged and fit, the sage rejoiced greatly. And his ancestors, O king, obtained the desired worlds.

sanskrit: agastyasyāśramaḥ khyātaḥ sarvartukusumānvitaḥ prāhrādir evaṃ vātāpir agastyena vināśitaḥ
english: The hermitage of Agastya is renowned, adorned with flowers of every season. Thus was Vātāpi, the descendant of Prahlāda, destroyed by Agastya.

sanskrit: tasyāyam āśramo rājan ramaṇīyo guṇair yutaḥ eṣā bhāgīrathī puṇyā yatheṣṭam avagāhyatām
english: This is his hermitage, O king, delightful and endowed with virtues. This is the sacred Bhāgīrathī — bathe in it to your heart's content.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhūya evāham icchāmi maharṣes tasya dhīmataḥ karmaṇāṃ vistaraṃ śrotum agastyasya dvijottama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "I wish to hear more at length of the deeds of that wise great sage Agastya, O best of twice-born men."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca śṛṇu rājan kathāṃ divyām adbhutām atimānuṣīm agastyasya mahārāja prabhāvam amitātmanaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: "Listen, O king, to a divine, wondrous, superhuman tale — O great king, the power of the immeasurable-souled Agastya."

sanskrit: āsan kṛtayuge ghorā dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ kāleyā iti vikhyātā gaṇāḥ paramadāruṇāḥ
english: In the Kṛta age there were terrible demons, frenzied for battle, known as the Kāleyas — groups of the most dreadful kind.

sanskrit: te tu vṛtraṃ samāśritya nānāpraharaṇodyatāḥ samantāt paryadhāvanta mahendrapramukhān surān
english: Taking refuge with Vṛtra, wielding all manner of weapons, they charged from all sides against the gods led by great Indra.

sanskrit: tato vṛtravadhe yatnam akurvaṃs tridaśāḥ purā puraṃdaraṃ puraskṛtya brahmāṇam upatasthire
english: Then the thirty gods, making effort for the slaying of Vṛtra, placing Purandara foremost, approached Brahmā.

sanskrit: kṛtāñjalīṃs tu tān sarvān parameṣṭhī uvāca ha viditaṃ me surāḥ sarvaṃ yad vaḥ kāryaṃ cikīrṣitam
english: The Lord of the highest heaven spoke to all of them as they stood with folded hands: "O gods, I know all that you wish to accomplish."

sanskrit: tam upāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathā vṛtraṃ vadhiṣyatha dadhīca iti vikhyāto mahān ṛṣir udāradhīḥ
english: "I shall tell you the means by which you will slay Vṛtra. There is a great sage known as Dadhīca, of noble intellect."

sanskrit: taṃ gatvā sahitāḥ sarve varaṃ vai saṃprayācata sa vo dāsyati dharmātmā suprītenāntarātmanā
english: "Go to him together, all of you, and beg a boon. That righteous-souled one, with his innermost heart delighted, will give it to you."

sanskrit: sa vācyaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvair bhavadbhir jayakāṅkṣibhiḥ svāny asthīni prayaccheti trailokyasya hitāya vai sa śarīraṃ samutsṛjya svāny asthīni pradāsyati
english: "He should be told by all of you together, you who desire victory: 'Give us your bones for the welfare of the three worlds.' He will surrender his body and bestow his own bones."

sanskrit: tasyāsthibhir mahāghoraṃ vajraṃ saṃbhriyatāṃ dṛḍham mahac chatruhaṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ṣaḍaśraṃ bhīmanisvanam
english: "From his bones, let a most terrible, firm thunderbolt be fashioned — mighty, enemy-slaying, sharp, six-edged, and with a fearsome sound."

sanskrit: tena vajreṇa vai vṛtraṃ vadhiṣyati śatakratuḥ etad vaḥ sarvam ākhyātaṃ tasmāc chīghraṃ vidhīyatām
english: "With that thunderbolt the Performer-of-a-hundred-sacrifices shall indeed slay Vṛtra. All of this has been told to you — therefore act quickly."

sanskrit: evam uktās tato devā anujñāpya pitāmaham nārāyaṇaṃ puraskṛtya dadhīcasyāśramaṃ yayuḥ
english: Thus instructed, the gods took leave of the Grandfather, placed Nārāyaṇa at their head, and went to Dadhīca's hermitage.

sanskrit: sarasvatyāḥ pare pāre nānādrumalatāvṛtam ṣaṭpadodgītaninadair vighuṣṭaṃ sāmagair iva puṃskokilaravonmiśraṃ jīvaṃjīvakanāditam
english: On the far bank of the Sarasvatī, covered with diverse trees and creepers, it rang with the melodious sounds of bees as if with the chanting of Sama singers, mingled with the calls of male cuckoos and resounding with the cries of jivamjivaka birds.

sanskrit: mahiṣaiś ca varāhaiś ca sṛmaraiś camarair api tatra tatrānucaritaṃ śārdūlabhayavarjitaiḥ
english: Buffalo, boar, sambar deer, and yaks wandered here and there without fear of tigers.

sanskrit: kareṇubhir vāraṇaiś ca prabhinnakaraṭāmukhaiḥ saro 'vagāḍhaiḥ krīḍadbhiḥ samantād anunāditam
english: It resounded on all sides with female elephants and bull elephants with faces streaming with ichor, who had waded into the lake and were at play.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghrair mahānādān nadadbhir anunāditam aparaiś cāpi saṃlīnair guhākandaravāsibhiḥ
english: It echoed with lions and tigers roaring mighty roars, and with others hidden and dwelling in caves and ravines.

sanskrit: teṣu teṣv avakāśeṣu śobhitaṃ sumanoramam triviṣṭapasamaprakhyaṃ dadhīcāśramam āgaman
english: Beautiful and most pleasing, adorned in all its various open spaces, resembling the heavenly realm — to that hermitage of Dadhīca they came.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyan dadhīcaṃ te divākarasamadyutim jājvalyamānaṃ vapuṣā yathā lakṣmyā pitāmaham
english: There they saw Dadhīca, blazing with the radiance of the sun, shining in his form just as the Grandfather shines with his glory.

sanskrit: tasya pādau surā rājann abhivādya praṇamya ca ayācanta varaṃ sarve yathoktaṃ parameṣṭhinā
english: The gods, O king, saluted his feet and bowed down, and all of them begged the boon just as the Supreme Lord had instructed.

sanskrit: tato dadhīcaḥ paramapratītaḥ; surottamāṃs tān idam abhyuvāca karomi yad vo hitam adya devāḥ; svaṃ cāpi dehaṃ tv aham utsṛjāmi
english: Then Dadhīca, supremely pleased, spoke thus to those best of gods: "I shall do today, O gods, what is beneficial to you — and I shall also abandon my own body."

sanskrit: sa evam uktvā dvipadāṃ variṣṭhaḥ; prāṇān vaśī svān sahasotsasarja tataḥ surās te jagṛhuḥ parāsor; asthīni tasyātha yathopadeśam
english: Having spoken thus, that best of two-footed beings, master of himself, suddenly released his vital breaths. Then those gods took his bones — his very marrow — according to instruction.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭarūpāś ca jayāya devās; tvaṣṭāram āgamya tam artham ūcuḥ tvaṣṭā tu teṣāṃ vacanaṃ niśamya; prahṛṣṭarūpaḥ prayataḥ prayatnāt
english: The gods, with joyful countenances and eager for victory, went to Tvaṣṭṛ and stated their purpose. Tvaṣṭṛ, hearing their words, was himself joyful of countenance and with great and careful effort —

sanskrit: cakāra vajraṃ bhṛśam ugrarūpaṃ; kṛtvā ca śakraṃ sa uvāca hṛṣṭaḥ anena vajrapravareṇa deva; bhasmīkuruṣvādya surārim ugram
english: — fashioned the thunderbolt, exceedingly fierce in form. Having fashioned it, he joyfully spoke to Śakra: "With this finest of thunderbolts, O god, reduce to ashes today the fierce enemy of the gods."

sanskrit: tato hatāriḥ sagaṇaḥ sukhaṃ vai; praśādhi kṛtsnaṃ tridivaṃ diviṣṭhaḥ tvaṣṭrā tathoktaḥ sa puraṃdaras tu; vajraṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ prayato 'bhyagṛhṇāt
english: "Then, your enemy and his hosts destroyed, rule happily and completely the triple heaven, O dweller in heaven." Thus instructed by Tvaṣṭṛ, Purandara joyfully and reverently accepted the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tataḥ sa vajrī balibhir daivatair abhirakṣitaḥ āsasāda tato vṛtraṃ sthitam āvṛtya rodasī
english: Lomaśa said: Then the bearer of the thunderbolt, protected by the mighty gods, encountered Vṛtra, who stood filling both heaven and earth.

sanskrit: kālakeyair mahākāyaiḥ samantād abhirakṣitam samudyatapraharaṇaiḥ saśṛṅgair iva parvataiḥ
english: He was guarded on all sides by the great-bodied Kāleyas, with weapons upraised, looking like mountains with their peaks.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavad devānāṃ saha dānavaiḥ muhūrtaṃ bharataśreṣṭha lokatrāsakaraṃ mahat
english: Then a great battle arose between the gods and the demons, a moment terrifying to all the worlds, O foremost of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: udyatapratipiṣṭānāṃ khaḍgānāṃ vīrabāhubhiḥ āsīt sutumulaḥ śabdaḥ śarīreṣv abhipātyatām
english: There arose an exceedingly tumultuous sound as swords raised and clashing in the arms of heroes fell upon bodies.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ prapatadbhiś ca antarikṣān mahītalam tālair iva mahīpāla vṛntād bhraṣṭair adṛśyata
english: With heads falling down from mid-air to the great earth, it looked, O lord of the earth, like palm fruits falling from their stalks.

sanskrit: te hemakavacā bhūtvā kāleyāḥ parighāyudhāḥ tridaśān abhyavartanta dāvadagdhā ivādrayaḥ
english: The Kāleyas, clad in golden armor and armed with iron clubs, charged against the thirty gods like mountains scorched by a forest fire.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vegavatāṃ vegaṃ sahitānāṃ pradhāvatām na śekus tridaśāḥ soḍhuṃ te bhagnāḥ prādravan bhayāt
english: The thirty gods could not withstand the onslaught of those swift ones charging together; broken, they fled in fear.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā dravato bhītān sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ vṛtre vivardhamāne ca kaśmalaṃ mahad āviśat
english: Seeing them fleeing in fear, and as Vṛtra waxed ever greater, the thousand-eyed Purandara was overcome by a great stupor.

sanskrit: taṃ śakraṃ kaśmalāviṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ svatejo vyadadhāc chakre balam asya vivardhayan
english: Seeing Śakra overcome by stupor, the eternal Viṣṇu poured his own energy into Śakra, augmenting his strength.

sanskrit: viṣṇunāpyāyitaṃ śakraṃ dṛṣṭvā devagaṇās tataḥ svaṃ svaṃ tejaḥ samādadhyus tathā brahmarṣayo 'malāḥ
english: Seeing Śakra replenished by Viṣṇu, the hosts of gods then infused their own respective energies into him, and likewise the pure brahmin-sages.

sanskrit: sa samāpyāyitaḥ śakro viṣṇunā daivataiḥ saha ṛṣibhiś ca mahābhāgair balavān samapadyata
english: Replenished thus by Viṣṇu together with the gods and the greatly blessed sages, Śakra became powerful again.

sanskrit: jñātvā balasthaṃ tridaśādhipaṃ tu; nanāda vṛtro mahato ninādān tasya praṇādena dharā diśaś ca; khaṃ dyaur nagāś cāpi cacāla sarvam
english: Knowing the lord of the thirty gods to be restored in strength, Vṛtra roared tremendous roars. At his roar, the earth and the directions, the sky, heaven, and mountains — all of it trembled.

sanskrit: tato mahendraḥ paramābhitaptaḥ; śrutvā ravaṃ ghorarūpaṃ mahāntam bhaye nimagnas tvaritaṃ mumoca; vajraṃ mahat tasya vadhāya rājan
english: Then great Indra, exceedingly tormented, upon hearing that mighty roar of terrible form, plunged into fear and swiftly hurled the great thunderbolt for his slaying, O king.

sanskrit: sa śakravajrābhihataḥ papāta; mahāsuraḥ kāñcanamālyadhārī yathā mahāñ śailavaraḥ purastāt; sa mandaro viṣṇukarāt pramuktaḥ
english: Struck by Śakra's thunderbolt, that great demon, wearing his golden garland, fell — just as the great mountain Mandara fell before, released from Viṣṇu's hand.

sanskrit: tasmin hate daityavare bhayārtaḥ; śakraḥ pradudrāva saraḥ praveṣṭum vajraṃ na mene svakarāt pramuktaṃ; vṛtraṃ hataṃ cāpi bhayān na mene
english: When that foremost of demons was slain, Śakra, overcome by fear, fled to enter a lake. Out of fear he did not acknowledge the thunderbolt discharged from his own hand, nor did he acknowledge Vṛtra as slain.

sanskrit: sarve ca devā muditāḥ prahṛṣṭā; maharṣayaś cendram abhiṣṭuvantaḥ sarvāṃś ca daityāṃs tvaritāḥ sametya; jaghnuḥ surā vṛtravadhābhitaptān
english: All the gods, delighted and joyful, together with the great sages praising Indra, quickly gathered and slew all the demons who were anguished at the slaying of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānās tridaśais tadānīṃ; samudram evāviviśur bhayārtāḥ praviśya caivodadhim aprameyaṃ; jhaṣākulaṃ ratnasamākulaṃ ca
english: Being slaughtered by the thirty gods at that time, they fled in fear and entered the ocean itself — plunging into the immeasurable sea, teeming with fish and filled with gems.

sanskrit: tadā sma mantraṃ sahitāḥ pracakrus; trailokyanāśārtham abhismayantaḥ tatra sma ke cin matiniścayajñās; tāṃs tān upāyān anuvarṇayanti
english: There, together, they took counsel, intent on the destruction of the three worlds. Some among them, knowing the determination of minds, enumerated those various strategies.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu tatra kramakālayogād; ghorā matiś cintayatāṃ babhūva ye santi vidyātapasopapannās; teṣāṃ vināśaḥ prathamaṃ tu kāryaḥ
english: Then, in due course of time and circumstance, a terrible resolve arose in those deliberating: "Those who are endowed with learning and austerity — their destruction must be accomplished first."

sanskrit: lokā hi sarve tapasā dhriyante; tasmāt tvaradhvaṃ tapasaḥ kṣayāya ye santi ke cid dhi vasuṃdharāyāṃ; tapasvino dharmavidaś ca tajjñāḥ teṣāṃ vadhaḥ kriyatāṃ kṣipram eva; teṣu pranaṣṭeṣu jagat pranaṣṭam
english: "For all the worlds are sustained by austerity; therefore hasten to destroy austerity. Whoever there are on this earth — the ascetics who know dharma and the sciences — let their slaughter be accomplished quickly. When they are destroyed, the world is destroyed."

sanskrit: evaṃ hi sarve gatabuddhibhāvā; jagadvināśe paramaprahṛṣṭāḥ durgaṃ samāśritya mahormimantaṃ; ratnākaraṃ varuṇasyālayaṃ sma
english: Thus all of them, their minds bent on destruction, supremely delighted in the annihilation of the world, took refuge in the stronghold of the great-waved ocean, the jewel-filled abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca samudraṃ te samāśritya vāruṇaṃ nidhim ambhasām kāleyāḥ saṃpravartanta trailokyasya vināśane
english: Lomaśa said: Taking refuge in the ocean, the treasury of Varuṇa's waters, the Kāleyas set about the destruction of the three worlds.

sanskrit: te rātrau samabhikruddhā bhakṣayanti sadā munīn āśrameṣu ca ye santi punyeṣv āyataneṣu ca
english: At night they would emerge in fury and continually devour the sages who dwelt in hermitages and in holy sanctuaries.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasyāśrame viprā bhakṣitās tair durātmabhiḥ aśītiśatam aṣṭau ca nava cānye tapasvinaḥ
english: At Vasiṣṭha's hermitage, eight thousand eight hundred brahmins were devoured by those evil-souled ones, and nine more ascetics besides.

sanskrit: cyavanasyāśramaṃ gatvā puṇyaṃ dvijaniṣevitam phalamūlāśanānāṃ hi munīnāṃ bhakṣitaṃ śatam
english: Going to Cyavana's hermitage, holy and frequented by twice-born ones, a hundred sages who lived on fruits and roots were devoured.

sanskrit: evaṃ rātrau sma kurvanti viviśuś cārṇavaṃ divā bharadvājāśrame caiva niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ vāyvāhārāmbubhakṣāś ca viṃśatiḥ saṃnipātitāḥ
english: Thus they would act at night and enter the ocean by day. At Bharadvaja's hermitage too, twenty disciplined celibate students who lived on air and water were struck down.

sanskrit: evaṃ krameṇa sarvāṃs tān āśramān dānavās tadā niśāyāṃ paridhāvanti mattā bhujabalāśrayāt kālopasṛṣṭāḥ kāleyā ghnanto dvijagaṇān bahūn
english: Thus, in this manner, the demons would range through all those hermitages at night, intoxicated with the power of their arms — those Kāleyas, driven by fate, slaughtering multitudes of twice-born men.
